label: prop:markov-gram-star-positive
title: The Markov--Gram star form is positive semidefinite; positivity reduces to $y_\lambda \ge 0$
html:
Let T_w^{*} = T_{w^{-1}} be the Hecke star and let

  S_{ij} \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(b_i\,b_j^{*}\bigr)

be the Gram matrix of the Markov trace on the normal-form basis b \in \{\gamma,\, \sigma_0,\, \sigma_1,\, L_+,\, L_-,\, e^{-}\} of H_3(q). Then S is positive semidefinite whenever every Wedderburn weight satisfies y_\lambda \ge 0, and its kernel is spanned by the blocks with y_\lambda = 0.

Positivity is a block computation, not a measurement

Wedderburn decomposes H_3(q) into matrix algebras, one per partition, and the Markov trace acts on the block of \lambda as y_\lambda times the matrix trace. The star form therefore splits as

  \mathrm{tr}_M(a\,a^{*}) \;=\; \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3} y_\lambda \cdot
  \mathrm{tr}\!\bigl(A_\lambda A_\lambda^{*}\bigr),

and on each M_d the sesquilinear trace \mathrm{tr}(AA^{*}) is the sum of the squares of the matrix entries. A nonnegative combination of sums of squares is nonnegative, and it vanishes only when every block with y_\lambda > 0 vanishes. Positivity of the whole form is thus equivalent to nonnegativity of the weights, and the degeneracy locus is exactly the set of blocks the trace kills.

Two consequences follow for H_3(q) without any numerical input.

  • Under convention C every weight is strictly positive, so S is positive definite: signature (6,0,0).
  • Under convention D the weight of (1^{3}) is zero, so S acquires a one-dimensional kernel and nothing else: signature (5,0,1).

The kernel under convention D is the row cap seen through the pairing. Quotienting by it leaves a genuine inner product, which is what a Rieffel Lipschitz seminorm requires.

The star is what makes the form positive

Positivity is a statement about the star pairing and about no other. The Hecke star sends the basis element of a word to the basis element of its inverse, which on the normal-form basis swaps L_+ \leftrightarrow L_- and fixes the remaining four vectors. That single swap flips the sign of the one antisymmetric direction in the mixed-symmetry block, and the sign it flips is the whole difference between the two pairings. The contrast is drawn in two pairings, two signatures, and no signature claim about the Markov--Gram form is meaningful until the pairing is named.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs --- real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here. At q_0 the star form has eigenvalues 0.855067 (fourfold), 0.101797 and 3.476950 under convention C, and 0, 0.752702 (threefold) and 4.230339 under convention D. The repeated magnitude under convention D is \mu_+ = 0.75270211325196540159, the T = 1 isospin projector scalar; the isolated 0.101797 under convention C is the (1^{3}) block, small because y_{(1^{3})} = 0.0227449 is small.
